title: Refusal reference
description: The seventeen refusal reasons, from reward_lens.core.reading.RefusalReason and REASON_MEANING, with the library's own remedy for each. Generated by scripts/build_catalogue.py. Seventeen and not sixteen: GROUND-TRUTH.md C-10 records that the library's own kernel page is one amendment behind, and two acceptance tests pin the enum at seventeen. A refusal is a value and a success in this library's semantics; nothing reading this file may style one as an error (HANDOFF.md rule 4).

whatToDo.description: Required, never optional. A refusal without a remedy is a tool that looks broken instead of a tool that looks honest, and guards.mjs requireRemedy throws on one.

remedy.description: Non-null on exactly the three reasons the library itself sorts. DECISIONS.md D-09: the mapping exists for three of seventeen and there is no code structure assigning a group to the other fourteen, so null is the honest value. Inventing fourteen classifications would be the site asserting a taxonomy its own subject does not hold, on the page whose subject is not asserting things you cannot support.

trustLadder.description: The library's TrustLevel enum, in rung order. The four display names come from copy.yaml:trust_ladder and never from a component; this file carries the enum, not the prose.

provenance.description: Which library this was read from. A libraryVersion below 3.0.0 means the generator ran under the wrong venv and every count is a v2 count; build_catalogue.py refuses that case rather than emitting it. skippedModules names the modules a missing optional extra kept out of the walk, and it is not decoration: an estimator registers when its module imports, so a skipped module makes its quantities read as open. A reader who is told which extras were missing can tell 'nobody has built this' from 'this build could not see it'.
